amoxicillin: Methotrexate: Reduced renal clearance increasing methotrexate toxicity risk.
Warfarin: May prolong INR through disruption of gut flora producing Vitamin K.
paracetamol: Chronic Alcohol Consumption: Potentiates CYP2E1 induction and hepatotoxicity.
Warfarin: Regular high-dose paracetamol may modestly elevate INR.
metformin: Iodinated Radiographic Contrast: Increases acute renal failure and lactic acidosis risk; hold for 48 hours.
Cimetidine / Dolutegravir: OCT2 inhibitors increase systemic metformin exposure.
atorvastatin: Clarithromycin / Ketoconazole: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase statin levels and rhabdomyolysis risk.
Gemfibrozil: Marked increase in statin-induced myopathy; avoid combination.
amlodipine: Simvastatin: Limit simvastatin dose to 20 mg daily due to CYP3A4 inhibition.
Cyclosporine / Tacrolimus: May increase calcineurin inhibitor blood levels.
telmisartan: Potassium Supplements / Spironolactone: Additive risk of severe hyperkalemia.
NSAIDs: Reduce antihypertensive effect and increase acute renal failure risk.
ramipril: Lithium: Decreased lithium excretion causing neurotoxicity.
NSAIDs: Blunts ACEi vasodilation and precipitates prerenal azotemia.
furosemide: Digoxin: Loop-induced hypokalemia markedly increases digitalis toxicity and arrhythmias.
Lithium: Reduced lithium clearance resulting in toxic accumulation.
ciprofloxacin: Theophylline: Potent CYP1A2 inhibition leads to toxic theophylline seizures.
Antacids / Iron / Calcium: Polyvalent cations chelate ciprofloxacin, eliminating oral bioavailability.
tramadol: SSRIs / SNRIs / Linezolid: High risk of life-threatening Serotonin Syndrome.
Carbamazepine: Enhances tramadol metabolism via CYP3A4, reducing analgesic efficacy.
clopidogrel: Omeprazole / Esomeprazole: CYP2C19 inhibition reduces clopidogrel active metabolite formation; prefer pantoprazole.
